summary: Mission Hill lookout in Chippewa County, Michigan, near Brimley: towermen in 1940 and 1948; an undated trail app describes the tower on the hilltop; no build date or height source found.

access.note: Trail and overlook on national forest land are described as open to hikers. No source says the tower itself is open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: 3.6-mile out-and-back trail along Spectacle Lake and Monocle Lake; trailhead and overlook on Tower Road.

events.note: May 1940 newspaper says a man from Brimley had returned to the Mission Hill tower, which he had occupied for several years

July 1948 newspaper: the family's cabin stood next to the tower and the report says the father was a towerman at the station; the same report describes a bear killing a forest ranger's three-year-old daughter a quarter mile from the cabin

notes_for_editor: History rests on two 1940 and 1948 newspaper items reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page. Today's status rests only on an undated commercial trail app that describes the tower in the present tense; treat standing status as unconfirmed. No build date, height or design found in any source; two web searches found none. The 1948 item calls the father a forest ranger in one sentence and a towerman in another; the story uses both. The 1948 item names the forest Marquette National Forest, while the listing uses Hiawatha; the story reports both without choosing. Staff and child names are left out on purpose.
